subject: Acme Cloud: technical onboarding brief + local SDK sprint plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Cloud: technical onboarding brief + local SDK sprint plan

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so engineering can start a local validation this week:

1) Goal: get a small local sandbox running that covers: text generation (Python), embeddings + similarity search, and a simple reranker flow (TypeScript sample). We also want one structured-output/tool-calling example (invoice extractor calling a simple webhook).

2) Constraints you mentioned: corporate dev machines are behind a restricted outbound proxy and we need a plan for short-lived service accounts (OIDC SAML) rather than long-lived API keys. Also: no direct internet egress from the staging subnet — we’ll rely on a NAT or VPC peered service.

Proposed plan (short timeline):
- Today: we’ll share a small artifacts bundle (SDK samples + docker-compose) and a one-page network checklist for your infra team.
- Fri (09/04): Karthik will send detailed quickstart commands for Python/TS and example env var configs for OIDC token exchange.
- Mon (09/07): run a 45-min pairing session to validate local dev + run the embeddings -> reranker flow against a small dataset.

Helpful notes for your engineers (high level):
- Python quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk; run sample_gen.py using LOCAL_MODE env. Sample will show streaming and structured output JSON schema.
- TypeScript quickstart: npm i @redwood/inference; ts-node samples/reranker.ts — the sample demonstrates embeddings-based candidate scoring and an optional fallback model.
- Auth: we recommend short-lived OIDC tokens exchanged for a short-lived Redwood access token via our token-exchange endpoint. If OIDC is blocked, we can provide a signed service account credential with 4-hour TTL as a fallback.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-sampleapps.tar.gz (samples + README), local-dev-docker-compose.yml, acme-network-requirements.pdf

If that plan looks good I’ll ask Marissa to schedule the pairing slot — what timezone window works best for your team next Monday?

Thanks —
Stephanie

--

Stephanie —

Thanks for the summary. That matches our ask. A few clarifications from infra:

- We cannot allow any inbound ports from the internet to our developer laptops. All traffic must originate from inside our VPC or via a secure bastion.
- OIDC: we use Okta and prefer OIDC token exchange. We'll need a short guide of the exact claim sets your token-exchange endpoint accepts (aud, sub, exp) so our IdP team can set up the app.
- Embeddings vector store: we will test locally with a small SQLite-backed vector store for the PoC. For the reranker, we'd like the sample to show how to swap Redwood-hosted embeddings -> local FAISS or SQLite.

For the pairing session Monday, our engineering leads are available 10:00–12:00 PT. Please keep the session focused (local run, auth handshake, embeddings demo).

Also can you confirm whether the sample apps will run with only outbound HTTPS (443) or if they require gRPC ports?

—Liam

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme Cloud: technical onboarding brief + local SDK sprint plan

Hi Liam —

Quick technical answers and copy-paste when you hand this to your IdP team. I kept this concise for the pairing:

Network / Ports:
- Outbound HTTPS (443) only is sufficient for the hosted Redwood API + token-exchange flow. Our SDK also supports HTTPS/REST over port 443. gRPC is optional — the sample uses REST.
- If you plan to run Redwood Private (VPC deployment) later, we’ll provide a separate gRPC endpoint but that’s not required for the PoC.

OIDC token exchange (recommended):
- Our token-exchange expects a standard OIDC id_token signed by your IdP (RS256). Required claims: iss, sub, aud (value: redwood-token-exchange), exp, iat.
- Exchange endpoint: https://auth.redwood.com/v1/exchange (POST)
- Example curl (replace placeholders):
  curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.com/v1/exchange -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"id_token":"<OKTA_ID_TOKEN>", "client_id":"acme-dev-01", "scopes":"inference:invoke"}'

- Successful response: {"access_token":"<short_lived_redwood_token>", "expires_in":3600}

Python quickstart (local mode):
- venv recommended
- pip install redwood-sdk==0.8.1
- ENV vars for local dev:
  REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.redwood.com
  REDWOOD_ACCESS_TOKEN=<short_lived_redwood_token>
  REDWOOD_LOCAL_MODE=true  # toggles sample to use local runner + no telemetry

- Run: python samples/text_gen_sample.py
- The sample shows streaming via server-sent events, plus a structured JSON schema example with tool_call: {"tool":"invoice_extractor","args":{}} that posts to localhost:8081/webhook. The webhook is included in the sample bundle.

TypeScript quickstart (reranker flow):
- Node 18+, npm install
- npm i @redwood/inference@0.8.1
- ENV vars: REDWOOD_BASE_URL, REDWOOD_ACCESS_TOKEN
- Run: node samples/reranker.js
- The TS sample includes:
  1) generate embeddings for a candidate set (calls /v1/embeddings)
  2) store vectors locally (small SQLite + in-memory index helper bundled)
  3) call the rerank endpoint with top-N candidates and use model.score output to reorder results

Local dev tooling:
- We included a docker-compose (local-dev-docker-compose.yml) that brings up: a small SQLite file server, a webhook receiver (invoice_extractor), and a local proxy that can simulate OIDC token issuance for offline work.
- Command to launch quickly:
  docker compose -f local-dev-docker-compose.yml up --build

Attachments in the bundle:
- redwood-sdk-sampleapps.tar.gz (samples/python, samples/ts, README)
- local-dev-docker-compose.yml
- acme-network-requirements.pdf (short checklist you can send to infra)

If you want, I can paste a minimal sample for the embedding call here; otherwise we'll walk through in the pairing. Confirm Monday 10–11 PT and I’ll block the slot.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
